ai.description: *Eutropis beddomei* is a small skink reaching 6 cm snout-vent length. It has a bronze-brown body with a distinct white mid-dorsal stripe and dark lateral bands. It features smooth scales and a pointed snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis beddomei* is best distinguished by the presence of a single pair of enlarged nuchal scales and a distinct, continuous pale dorsolateral stripe bordered by black.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis beddomei* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in peninsular India, typically found at elevations ranging from near sea level up to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Beddome's Mabuya is a diurnal skink that actively forages for small insects among leaf litter and rocky outcrops, often basking in sunlit patches to regulate its temperature.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis beddomei* is ovoviviparous, typically producing a litter of 3–5 young. Breeding occurs primarily during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis beddomei* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily inhabiting the Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
